extra.message: User-supplied JSON body is deserialized and merged via .update() into a server-side dictionary that controls authorization attributes (role, tier, approved, balance). This allows mass assignment of privilege-escalating fields.

Access-Control-Allow-Origin is set to reflect the incoming Origin header, and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to 'true'. This allows any website to make credentialed cross-origin requests, enabling credential theft.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The acct_identity_ping_333 endpoint has no _wrk_gate() authentication check, unlike every other partner_console endpoint. It is accessible without any authentication header.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Known handles and verifier secrets are hardcoded in source code. Different response messages for 'unknown handle' (404) vs 'bad verifier' (403) allow handle enumeration. The verifier comparison is not constant-time, enabling timing attacks.

SSL certificate verification is explicitly disabled using ssl._create_unverified_context(), and combined with urllib.request.urlopen(). This allows man-in-the-middle attacks on outbound HTTPS requests.
Response headers explicitly disable XSS protection (X-XSS-Protection: 0) and clear the Content-Security-Policy, removing client-side security protections.

The 'safe_break' template filter uses mark_safe() on user-controllable content without HTML escaping. It is used in multiple templates to render escalation summaries, comments, organization notes, and deal notes — all of which are user-authored fields. This allows stored XSS attacks.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: SSN and credit card numbers are read from GET query parameters and written to a file. GET parameters are logged in browser history, server access logs, and appear in referrer headers, exposing sensitive financial/PII data.
